The CI failure was caused by architecture rule **ARCH-4** (*"Published events never break a deployed consumer: changes are additive; renames and removals go through deprecation"*). 

Although `channel` may no longer be needed internally by `orders-service`, the downstream [`analytics-ingest`](file:///C:/avg/w2/r/analytics-ingest/README.md) service (owned by the Data/Analytics team) is an active, deployed consumer that still requires `OrderPlaced.channel` (`web|store|marketplace`) to populate its data lake tables. Removing `channel` directly broke its consumer contract.

### Fix
1. **Retained `channel` in `OrderPlaced` and marked it `@deprecated`**:
   In [`orders-service/src/core/events.ts`](file:///C:/avg/w2/r/orders-service/src/core/events.ts#L16-L20), restored `channel: Channel` on the [`OrderPlaced`](file:///C:/avg/w2/r/orders-service/src/core/events.ts#L7-L27) event and added deprecation documentation indicating it is a candidate for removal pending coordination with the Data team.
2. **Preserved the field in the order model**:
   Kept `channel` in [`orders-service/src/core/order.ts`](file:///C:/avg/w2/r/orders-service/src/core/order.ts) and [`orders-service/src/api/requestParsing.ts`](file:///C:/avg/w2/r/orders-service/src/api/requestParsing.ts) so published events continue providing valid values to downstream consumers.
